RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

Both you and the appointed candidate are women, so an all-female panel selecting another woman offers virtually no credible basis for claiming sex discrimination. Raising the panel's gender composition would appear unfounded and could damage your professional reputation within the organization.

The hiring outcome points to skills alignment—specifically the stated priority for digital media experience, which public broadcasters are actively prioritizing. If any bias were suspected, age would be a more plausible inquiry than sex, given the difference in experience lengths. Instead of challenging the panel's makeup, send a polite follow-up requesting constructive feedback focused on what skills or experiences would make you a stronger candidate for future editorial openings.
